A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniLIP work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A-F support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original UniLIP reconstruction, understanding, generation, and editing results, together with quantitative ablations and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds reasoning-editing evaluations, ImageNet probes, architectural comparisons, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The original reconstruction training and dual-condition architecture remain unchanged. Appendix C.7 adds UniLIP-JanusFlow, replacing JanusFlow's SigLIP and SDXL-VAE encoders with reconstruction-trained UniLIP-SigLIP and a single 576-token representation. This is a limited architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: Appendices B.4-B.5 add RISE evaluations requiring temporal, causal, spatial, and logical reasoning in editing, plus ImageNet classification through linear and attentive probes. ImageNet previously supported reconstruction evaluation. The original training corpora and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 16-17 introduce JanusFlow as an evaluated comparator, including its adaptation for editing with concatenated SigLIP and VAE features. Comparator membership in the corresponding original benchmark tables is unchanged; DreamLLM's addition concerns attribution rather than a new evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands the evaluation design with linear and attentive probing, a query-length sweep from 0 to 512, an editing-only training control, and paired JanusFlow variants fine-tuned on ShareGPT-4o-Image for 10k steps. The originally reported main training budgets, resolutions, learning rates, and guidance settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's existing ablations and reconstruction curve, v3 adds single-stage versus two-stage convergence comparisons, a classification-loss alternative, decoded-query case studies, query-length sensitivity, joint versus editing-only training, and unified versus dual-encoder analysis in JanusFlow. These substantially deepen investigation of training stability, query behavior, and architectural generality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new tables and curves continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original scores are retained, including 0.90 GenEval, 0.63 WISE, and 3.94 ImgEdit. Substantial new results include RISE overall scores of 8.1 for UniLIP-3B versus BAGEL's 6.1, ImageNet probe scores of 79.5/82.4 versus frozen CLIP's 79.8/82.6, and JanusFlow comparison scores of 0.75/0.36/3.09 versus 0.73/0.31/2.95 on GenEval/WISE/ImgEdit. New convergence, ablation, and qualitative findings further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The reconstruction relation, reconstruction and self-distillation objectives, and adversarial objective in Appendix A.4 are unchanged. The additions are empirical analyses and explanations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about preserving CLIP understanding while enabling reconstruction, generation, and editing through two-stage training and dual conditioning. Their headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking decoder pre-alignment to training stability, decoded queries to inferred image content, longer queries to increased reasoning capacity, and generation data to reduced editing overfitting. Appendix C.7 attributes benefits to eliminating dual-encoder feature misalignment. The loss discussion now explains classification loss's weakness through coarse supervision; Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.7 documents the new variant's encoder choices, pretrained initialization, fine-tuning dataset and duration, and 1152-versus-576 token counts. Appendix C.4 describes interpreting query outputs as text embeddings. Existing implementation details, hardware disclosures, and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 separates unified tokenizers from unified architectures and explicitly credits DreamLLM with introducing the learnable-query bridge before MetaQuery. DreamLLM, Janus, and JanusFlow references are added, while SynerGen-VL and LlamaFusion references are removed. The overarching positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Part of related work is rewritten, and the existing generation/editing training description is expanded into Section 3.3. Additional appendix subsections, acknowledgments, affiliations, contact details, and the conference header are introduced. Most original prose, including the abstract and conclusion, is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds a comparative convergence plot and a decoded-query/image comparison grid in Figures 6 and 8, expands Table 11, and introduces Tables 12-17 for the new evaluations and analyses. The original reconstruction curve becomes Figure 7; original full benchmark Tables 12-14 become Tables 18-20. Existing image galleries are retained with renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the central design choices and applicability beyond the original backbone. The paired JanusFlow comparison and independent ImageNet probes address gaps in architectural generality and semantic-preservation evidence, while convergence, query-length, and joint-training controls better explain the method's benefits. Some new protocols remain sparsely documented and causal interpretations exceed what the comparisons establish, but the added controls and clearer attribution provide a substantial overall quality gain.
